pages.text: A condensate of density n carries sound at c = √(gn/m). It flows at v toward a step of depth U that speeds it to √(v² + 2kU/m) and thins it, so beyond the step it outruns its own sound: a horizon. There the flow speeds up over about a healing length, giving a surface gravity κ, and phonon pairs appear across the horizon at T_H = ħκ/2πk_B. They show only against a condensate colder than that, summed over many shots.
$(thing)Set$(): Density, Upstream flow, Step depth, Shots.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Shot-to-shot atom number: the density varies by ±3%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): The trap is too warm for a condensate to form.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Fewer shots are faster.

$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Sound speed before: c = √(gn/m)$(br)Flow after the step: v₂ = √(v² + 2kU/m)$(br)Sound speed after: c₂ = c·√(n₂/n)$(br)Mach number before: v/c$(br)Mach number after: v₂/c₂$(br)Hawking temperature: T_H = ħκ/2πk_B$(br)Condensate temperature: T_c
